receipt.public_excerpt: Microsoft has been sued by shareholders who accused the company of defrauding them and inflating its stock price by failing to disclose slowing growth in its Azure cloud business

evidence_items.explanation: A pending class action naming Nadella alleges misleading disclosures. As reported, it focuses on Azure growth and AI spending, not on AI revenue concentration. Microsoft calls the claims without merit, and there is no finding.

receipt.public_excerpt: Set against Satya Nadella's earlier claim that the AI business was on a $37 billion annual run rate at the end of the March quarter, that implies OpenAI is driving more than half, and possibly around 70%

evidence_items.explanation: Shows that OpenAI's share of Microsoft's AI revenue was large: an implied ratio, not a disclosed figure. It does not show that any Nadella statement was false or misleading.

receipt.public_excerpt: The company never disclosed OpenAI‘s backlog outright. Instead, Hood told analysts that commercial RPO “increased 25% when excluding OpenAI.”

evidence_items.explanation: Microsoft gave investors OpenAI-excluded growth figures. That cuts against a charge of hiding concentration, though it was not a full breakdown.

receipt.public_excerpt: only Microsoft has disclosed a point-in-time share: OpenAI was about 45% of RPO in December

evidence_items.explanation: Microsoft told investors OpenAI's share of its backlog in January 2026. That counts against the claim that investors were kept in the dark about concentration.

unresolved_gaps: No court, regulator, or company finding that Nadella misled investors about AI revenue concentration; the class action is pending.
